note: Initial values of the mix-stage planner (core/mixplan.py; docs/SPEC.md 6.5, 6.8, 7.2). Every number here is a practice-level starting point and a calibration target, not a specification. Rules cited: R-04 order, R-05 cut before boost, R-06 small EQ moves, R-07 HPF below the lowest f0, R-08 low-band roles, R-09 low-end mono by measured loss, R-11 times in note values, R-12 minimum phase / octave widths, R-13 dynamic vs static, R-22 separated / baked stems, R-28 the lower-importance side yields, R-29 opposite safety valves.

template_mapping.note: SPEC 6.5.4 five-stage vocal template mapped onto the fixed order of 6.5.1 (a mapping, not a reordering): stage 1 and stage 4 are cuts (step 3), stage 2 is dynamics (step 4), stage 3 is additive (step 5), stage 5 is space (step 6).

acceptance.note: A candidate is scored by the resolved objective (objectives.evaluate, level matched) plus the stage guard terms (penalties of P-10, P-02 vs_lead and P-22, weighted as here) because the mix stage acts on exactly these (R-05, R-28) even when the chosen objective does not weigh them. Corrective moves are kept when the total improves by min_improvement, or when their target metric improves by min_target_gain while the total worsens by at most template_tolerance. Template moves (SPEC 6.5.4 defaults, rule-based HPFs) are kept unless they worsen the total by more than template_tolerance. A constraint failure, a newly failing OF-5 check or undoing a problem solved in an earlier step always rejects.

static_balance.note: P-10 aim = low edge + p10_aim_fraction x (target width) of the genre prior band (knowledge/genre_priors.json p10_target_db, else the generic band). R-05: the accompaniment is trimmed first, importance-aware (trim weight = lead importance - stem importance + importance_floor, normalised to the largest), up to accompaniment_max_trim_db for the least important stem; the lead is raised only for the rest, up to lead_raise_max_db. A floating lead is lowered (a cut) up to lead_cut_max_db.

pan.note: Only centred, near-mono harmony stems are spread off the lead's centre (LC/RC presets + fine). Low end and the lead stay centred (R-09). The masking model averages channels, so spatial release from masking is not credited by P-02; pan moves are kept as rule-based defaults within tolerance.

arrangement.note: Suggestions only (remix operations of SPEC 9.3, applied by a human or agent): range mute / level drop of the lower-importance masker where it overlaps the lead when the lead stays buried by more than min_buried_db (R-28); band-owner rotation per section when a P-22 band has more than p22_max_owners owners; a role check when a non-lead vocal stem carries clearly more clarity-band energy than the lead.

eq.note: R-06: one move stays within +-3 dB; the summed response of the planner's moves at any band centre stays within max_cumulative_db (beyond that, verification and a recorded reason are required, so the planner does not go there). Widths are octaves (R-12).

competitor_cut.note: R-05: the competitor is cut at the lead's strongest frequency inside the masked region (P-02 vs_lead regions: low-mid 200-800 Hz, presence 2-5 kHz).

accompaniment_yield.note: SPEC 6.5.4 stage 4: the accompaniment's 1-3 kHz is lowered 1.5-2 dB to make room for the core of the voice (R-05). -2 dB when the lead is still below its P-10 aim or masked in the presence region. Rhythm core and low end are not asked to yield by default. Opposite valve (R-29): the accompaniment presence (1-4 kHz) may not drop more than accompaniment_presence_max_drop_db.

lead_subtractive.note: SPEC 6.5.4 stage 1 (initial values 200-400 Hz and 2.5-6 kHz, 2-4 dB) adapted by measurement: a cut is placed only where the lead's 1/6-octave level exceeds its 1-octave smoothed level by the min excess; the depth is cut_fraction x excess, capped at 3 dB by R-06. Never inside the lead's fundamental range (lowest f0 - core_margin_oct .. median f0 + core_upper_oct octaves): a peak there is the core of the voice, not mud (6.8.1 'futoi', R-29).

low_band_role.note: R-08: when more than low_end.max_elements stems own the sub or bass band (P-22), the stems that are not the low-end owners yield with a low shelf (not a steeper HPF: R-07 keeps HPFs below the lowest f0).

hpf.note: R-07: cutoff = min(margin_ratio x lowest f0, the frequency below which spectral_floor_fraction of the stem's energy lies, role max). The lowest f0 is used only above f0_confidence_min; otherwise the spectral floor alone decides. Vocals: SPEC 6.5.4 stage 1 initial 80-100 Hz. Below min_cutoff_hz no filter is placed. Paired with the low-energy floor monitor (low_end).

low_end.note: R-08: 1-2 simultaneous low-band elements. R-29: a low cut may not lower the mix low/rest ratio (P-07, 20-250 Hz) by more than low_floor_max_drop_db; when it would, the cutoffs are relaxed once, then the move is dropped.

compressor.note: SPEC 6.5.3 yardsticks (knowledge/thresholds.json compressor_gr_yardsticks): 1-2 dB light glue, 3-6 dB evens the grain, above 10 dB excessive. SPEC 6.5.4 stage 2: fast peak control then slow 2-3 dB levelling. Thresholds are solved from the measured gain reduction of the reference compressor; makeup restores the measured active level so the step-1 balance holds. Release times are chosen as note values at the project tempo (R-11).

deesser.note: Placed on the lead when its own P-17 (5-8 kHz events vs 1-4 kHz) has a positive penalty. Dynamic, because sibilance is intermittent (R-13). Opposite valve (R-29, consonant clarity floor): the average 5-8 kHz level of the lead may not drop more than max_band_drop_db.

ducking.note: Time-axis unmasking (P-02 time_axis) as gain automation on the bass (SPEC 9.2 v1 automation = gain) keyed by the kick onsets: no sidechain input exists in v1. Triggered when the kick is buried by the bass beyond the P-02 time_axis ok range, or when the objective weighs the time axis. The release is the suggested note value of the time_axis measurement (R-11).

saturation.note: SPEC 6.5.4 stage 3: harmonics in 1-5 kHz keep the voice present on small speakers (OF-5 band-limited check). A parallel blend (mix < 1) approximates the band-limited saturation of the template; the measured change of the lead's 1-5 kHz share is recorded. Bass enhancement only when OF-5 check 4 (pitch without the fundamental) fails or P-08 is poor.

reverb.note: SPEC 6.5.4 stage 5: plate-like (dense, few distinct early reflections), the return low-cut at 600 Hz and high-cut at 6 kHz keep only the tail. Depth order (P-09): the lead gets the lowest send (dry = front), harmony more, pads/fx most; rhythm core and low end stay dry. With a declared depth order the sends rise by declared_order_step_db per rank. Pre-delay is chosen as a note value (R-11).

interest.note: R-26: the planner does not create interest; it only reports when the section contrast (P-20, quiet vs loud short-term loudness) dropped by more than contrast_max_drop_db between the starting static mix and the proposal.

mix_bus.note: Light glue only (1-2 dB). A low-band mono split is added only when S-03 / S-04 fail on the measured mix (R-09), never by default.

r22.note: R-22: separated stems (asset origin 'separated') and baked stems (peak within 0.5 dB of full scale and peak-to-loudness ratio below 8 dB: processed, no headroom) are used for balance only: gain within +-max_gain_change_db, pan unchanged (bleed from other parts moves with it), no EQ / dynamics / spatial processing. A track's declared restrictions.operations always wins.

vocabulary_en.note: English labels for report sentences when knowledge/vocabulary.json has no English word; translation by band + phenomenon (SPEC 6.8.1 rule 5).
